content: YouTube ToS explicitly prohibits downloading content via third-party tools outside the official player/embeds. yt-dlp itself is legal software (open source tool), but using it against YouTube's ToS is a contract violation (civil/account-level risk, not criminal). Risk is heightened when a service extracts audio and stores/serves derived clips to multiple users rather than pure personal ephemeral use. Practical implication: build clip caching/serving conservatively (short clips, not full tracks; require host-owned content assertion) and always keep the manual upload fallback as a ToS-safer path.
